aboutGame.title: What is ForgeTax?
paragraphs: ForgeTax is a blacksmith roguelite built around one clean idea: you run a fantasy forge, and a dragon expects to be paid. Each run has you gather ore, heat metal, hammer out swords, roll their stats, and sell the results to adventurers before the dragon's forge tax comes due.

Between runs you reinvest into better tools, higher material tiers, and stronger blades. Great Successes and lucky stat rolls turn a decent sword into a carry weapon, while a missed tax payment ends the run in ash. Short repeatable sessions and permanent unlocks make every failed attempt feed the next one.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Quick answers to the most common questions about ForgeTax.

items.question: What is ForgeTax?
items.answer: ForgeTax is a blacksmith roguelite about running a fantasy forge. You gather ore, hammer swords, roll their stats, sell the results to adventurers, and race to pay the dragon's forge tax before the run ends.

items.question: How does the dragon's forge tax work?
items.answer: The dragon collects a recurring fee that acts as the run's timer. Set aside enough gold for the payment before you spend on one more reroll, or the run ends in ash.

items.question: What are Great Successes in ForgeTax?
items.answer: A Great Success is a rare, high-quality outcome while forging or upgrading. It usually delivers the biggest single jump in a weapon's worth, so chase it on your strongest blade.

items.question: Should I upgrade every sword in ForgeTax?
items.answer: No. Pick one weapon per run as your carry and pour upgrades into it. Keep a cheap backup for customer orders, and salvage any blade that falls below your carry.

items.question: Which platforms does ForgeTax support?
items.answer: ForgeTax targets PC and is tracked through its Steam store page, where you can wishlist it and follow developer updates. Check the official listing for the current demo and launch details.
